top_story_title: Arista patches actively exploited VeloCloud Orchestrator zero-day: a read-only login becomes full SD-WAN operator
top_story_summary: Arista Networks released security updates on 22 October 2026 for a zero-day in VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO) On-Prem, the central management system for VeloCloud SD-WAN. The flaw is an SQL injection that, according to Arista's advisory as reported, lets anyone who can authenticate to the orchestrator - including a read-only customer account - escalate to operator, the highest level of control over the platform. Arista says it is being exploited in attacks.
top_actions: Inventory on-prem VeloCloud Orchestrator instances and determine which are reachable from anything other than a management network or VPN.
Apply Arista's VeloCloud Orchestrator update - the collected reporting does not state a fixed build, so check the vendor advisory for the fixed release before scheduling the change.
Audit the orchestrator user list for operator and admin accounts nobody recognises, and remove or downgrade read-only accounts that are no longer needed - the flaw escalates from exactly those.
Rotate orchestrator admin credentials, API tokens and service-account passwords after the upgrade; a pre-patch escalation survives the patch.
Diff SD-WAN edge templates and recent config pushes against a known-good baseline, looking for changed tunnel policy, firewall rules, DNS servers or route overrides.
executive_summary: Arista is patching an actively exploited SQL injection zero-day in on-prem VeloCloud Orchestrator that promotes a read-only customer login to full operator control of the SD-WAN fleet - patch, then audit the operator account list.

Cisco published a batch of Snort 3 advisories: a hardening release for out-of-bounds writes (CVE-2026-20043) plus five detection-engine denial-of-service flaws, one of which can cause inspection bypass rather than a restart depending on configuration.
PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) has reached network vendors - Cisco opened a Critical product-impact advisory and Palo Alto Networks a High one, both still enumerating affected products.

Check Point Research reports PHP2Shell exploitation attempts against 10% of organisations worldwide after details leaked ahead of disclosure, with government sites in the Netherlands and Finland taken offline as a precaution.
No collected item in this window carried a CISA KEV listing, and no EPSS scores were returned for the CVEs present.
Fixed releases: none of the collected advisories state a fixed build in the harvested text - check each vendor advisory before scheduling a change window.
key_actions: **Arista** — Locate every on-prem VCO instance, including lab and staging servers, and record the running version.
**Arista** — Apply Arista's update; check the vendor advisory for the fixed release, which the collected reporting does not state.
**Arista** — Patch VCO first, ahead of edge devices, then validate certificate trust across the fabric - check the vendor advisory for the fixed release.
**Arista** — Enumerate every read-only and customer account on the orchestrator and disable the ones that are dormant, shared or belong to third parties.
**Cisco** — Identify every device running Snort 3 from your inventory - firewall model plus running software and SRU/LSP version.
**Cisco** — Check the Cisco advisory for the fixed release per product, then plan a single upgrade that also covers the other October Snort 3 advisories rather than six separate windows.
**Cisco** — Bookmark the Cisco advisory and re-check it daily until the affected product list is published - it is explicitly marked as being updated.
**Cisco** — In the meantime, remove web management interfaces of Cisco appliances from internet reachability and restrict them to management networks by ACL.

headlines.title: Arista patches new VeloCloud Orchestrator zero-day exploited in attacks
headlines.summary: Arista released updates for a zero-day in VeloCloud Orchestrator On-Prem that attackers are already exploiting against SD-WAN management servers.

headlines.title: Arista Warns of Critical VeloCloud SQL Injection Zero-Day Exploited in Attacks
headlines.summary: An SQL injection zero-day in Arista's VeloCloud Orchestrator lets any authenticated user, even read-only, escalate to operator over the whole SD-WAN fabric.

headlines.title: Multiple Cisco Products Snort 3 Security Hardening Release: October 2026
headlines.summary: Cisco shipped a Snort 3 hardening release for out-of-bounds write flaws (CVE-2026-20043) found in its own internal review of the detection engine.

headlines.title: Vulnerabilities in PHP Affecting Cisco Products: October 2026
headlines.summary: Cisco opened a Critical advisory assessing which of its products are exposed to the PHP2Shell RCE pair, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619.

headlines.title: Multiple Cisco Products Snort 3 Generic Routing Encapsulation Denial of Service Vulnerability
headlines.summary: Improper handling of nested GRE traffic in Cisco's Snort 3 engine can restart inspection or, depending on configuration, let traffic bypass it entirely.

headlines.title: CVE-2026-109618 Impact of Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) on Palo Alto Networks Products (Severity: HIGH)
headlines.summary: Palo Alto Networks opened a High-severity advisory on the impact of the PHP2Shell RCE pair, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, on its products.
